title: What Is a Semantic Layer
description: A semantic layer translates physical tables into the metrics, dimensions and relationships a business actually asks about, and the definitions run rather than sit in a wiki.
beats: Tables on one side, questions on the other
One machine-readable layer in between
Definitions, plus the machinery around them
The definitions execute, they are not documentation

title: Metrics, Dimensions, Relationships
description: Inside a semantic model: metrics carry their own filters and time logic, dimensions are the ways you slice them, and declared relationships are what keep generated joins from double counting.
beats: A metric is a number with its rules attached
Dimensions are the ways a metric is sliced
Declare the entities once, join them correctly forever
Undeclared joins are how totals silently inflate

title: Governed Metrics
description: Metric logic scattered across tools drifts until meetings become arguments about whose number is real. A governed semantic layer makes the definition singular, reviewable and enforceable.
beats: One metric name, six different answers
Logic copied forward, edited under deadline
Treat a definition like code, because it is
Governance you can audit, not hope for

title: How a Semantic Query Resolves
description: Resolve, generate, optimize, enforce. Understanding those four steps is enough to read any semantic layer's architecture page, because the products differ in where the steps run, not in what they are.
beats: Turn names into a plan
Compile the plan into engine SQL
Answer from a materialization when one fits
Apply the rules before results leave

title: Headless BI
description: When the semantic model lives inside one BI tool, only that tool is governed. Headless BI runs the model as a service so dashboards, notebooks, apps and agents all resolve against the same definitions.
beats: Semantics trapped inside one tool
The model becomes a service, not a feature
Whatever the consumer already speaks
Swap the front end, keep the meaning

title: Semantic Layers and AI Agents
description: MCP can connect an agent to your data in an afternoon, and what it finds on the other side decides whether the answer is trustworthy. Raw schemas produce confident guesses; governed metrics produce endorsed numbers.
beats: The protocol connects, it does not explain
What the agent finds decides the answer
Grounding is what closes the accuracy gap
Your semantic layer is a knowledge interface

title: Apache Ossie
description: Apache Ossie, incubating at the ASF and formerly Open Semantic Interchange, is a vendor-neutral specification for metrics, dimensions and relationships, so semantic definitions can move between BI, analytics and AI platforms.
beats: Lock-in has been unwinding one layer at a time
Years of business logic in a private format
A neutral spec for metrics and dimensions
From an industry initiative to an Apache project

title: The Semantic Lakehouse
description: The lakehouse opened up files, tables and catalogs. Putting the semantic layer next to that open data is what turns storage everyone can read into answers everyone can trust.
beats: The lakehouse opened the stack underneath
An open table is still not a definition
Put the semantics next to the data
Open underneath, governed on top
